structure.note: Three classes: Class B carries ten votes per share, Class A one vote and Class C none. The FY2024 10-K says Larry Page and Sergey Brin together beneficially owned about 87.4% of Class B, about 52.1% of the voting power, at December 31, 2024. The 2025 proxy gives Page 27.1% and Brin 25.2% of total voting power. No single person holds a majority, so 'controlled' is false, but the two co-founders together do.

notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2024. Documents read on sec.gov: FY2024 Form 10-K (accession 0001652044-25-000014) and 2025 proxy statement (DEF 14A, accession 0001308179-25-000511). OWNERSHIP: the proxy table covers only the voting classes (A and B); 'Non-voting Class C capital stock is not included in the table.' Page's 389,051,160 Class B shares are 45.5% of Class B and 27.1% of total voting power. The economic share is therefore given only as leader.derived (3.20%), computed from his Class B shares over all three classes outstanding on the April 8, 2025 record date, both taken from the proxy. It counts Class B only, so it is a floor: if Page holds any Class C, which neither filing discloses, his economic stake is higher. LARGEST HOLDERS left empty on purpose: the proxy's 5% holders are stated only as percentages of a class (The Vanguard Group 493,782,758 Class A = 8.5% of Class A, based on a 13G/A filed Feb 14, 2024; BlackRock 415,076,460 Class A = 7.1% of Class A, 13G/A filed Feb 1, 2024; Eric E. Schmidt 5.6% of Class B; Sergey Brin 362,766,628 Class B = 42.4% of Class B, 25.2% of voting power), with Class C excluded, so none of them is a share of all shares outstanding and recomputing them is not allowed. STOCK COMP: the cash-flow line ($22,785 million) is used; the Note 13 text gives total SBC expense of $22.8 billion, of which $22.0 billion relates to awards expected to settle in Alphabet stock. DIVIDENDS: the first dividends were paid in June 2024 ($3.5 billion Class A, $519 million Class B, $3.3 billion Class C). GEOGRAPHY: copied as reported, including the hedging line; EMEA = Europe, Middle East and Africa, APAC = Asia-Pacific, Other Americas = Canada and Latin America. No broad employee stock purchase plan is described, so plan is null. Structure note source (FY2024 10-K, Item 1A): 'As of December 31, 2024, Larry Page and Sergey Brin beneficially owned approximately 87.4% of our outstanding Class B stock, which represented approximately 52.1% of the voting power of our outstanding common stock.'

ecosystem.notes: Alphabet reports no gross flow volume for its platforms, so measure is null. payouts is TAC: FY2024 TAC was $54.9B. The 10-K defines it as amounts paid to distribution partners (browser providers, mobile carriers, OEMs, software developers) and to Google Network partners. The TAC rate is 20.7% of advertising revenues, as stated in the 10-K. platformRevenue is Google advertising revenues ($264.59B) because TAC is measured against advertising. Total Alphabet revenues were $350.018B. YouTube creator payments are not in TAC. The 10-K puts them inside 'content acquisition costs' in other cost of revenues and gives no separate amount. The YouTube $100B figure is company-reported, covers four years in total (Jan 2021–Dec 2024) and is not an FY2024 flow. Its source URL is on services.google.com, Google's own file host; the records validator's search-page check (/google\./) would wrongly flag it.
